served.stem: Aniline is dissolved in diethyl ether along with a neutral hydrocarbon impurity. To extract the aniline into the aqueous phase as a water-soluble salt, which reagent should be added during the acid/base extraction?
served.bankWhy: Aniline is a base; aqueous HCl protonates the amine to water-soluble anilinium chloride, pulling it into the aqueous layer. NaOH/NaHCO3 are basic and leave the neutral amine in ether; brine and MgSO4 do not ionize it.

answer.line: Aniline is a base. Acid turns it into anilinium chloride, a salt, and salts move into water while the neutral impurity stays in the ether.

steps: Name what aniline is: a weak base, with a lone pair on N ready for a proton.
To charge a base, add an acid. Aqueous HCl protonates the nitrogen and makes anilinium chloride.
Charged things go to the water layer. The neutral hydrocarbon has nothing to grab a proton with, so it stays in the ether on top.

choices.note: Bicarbonate is the wash that pulls a carboxylic acid out of ether. Aniline stays neutral with a base, so it stays put.
Acid charges the base: anilinium chloride moves into the water.
Brine pulls dissolved water out of the organic layer and breaks emulsions. It changes no charges, so it separates nothing here.
MgSO4 dries the organic layer at the end of a workup. It is a solid drying agent and moves nothing into water.
NaOH deprotonates acids, like phenols and carboxylic acids. A base needs the opposite, an acid, to become a salt.

student.lockIt: To pull a compound into water, charge it: acid for an amine, base for an acid.
